subject: Chemistry
title: Phage Therapy: Viruses vs. Bacteria
description: A fast breakdown of Phage Therapy: Viruses vs. Bacteria for builders.

hook.text: Bacteriophages are viruses that kill bacteria. As antibiotic resistance grows, we're rediscovering them as medicine.

buildup.text: Phages inject DNA into bacteria, hijack their machinery, and multiply until the bacterium bursts—releasing hundreds of new phages.

discovery.text: Each phage targets one bacterial species precisely. Unlike antibiotics, phages don't harm beneficial gut bacteria.

twist.text: The Soviet Union used phage therapy for decades while the West chose antibiotics. Georgian pharmacies still sell phage cocktails.

climax.text: In 2019, phages saved a teenager dying from antibiotic-resistant Mycobacterium. It was the first IV phage therapy in the US.

punchline.text: Viruses that kill bacteria on demand. An old idea may solve the resistance crisis.

quiz.question: What advantage do phages have over traditional antibiotics?
options: Each phage targets one bacterial species precisely without harming beneficial bacteria
Phages are cheaper to produce than any antibiotic
Bacteria cannot develop resistance to phage attacks

details.summary: Phage therapy uses bacteriophages, viruses that naturally infect and kill specific bacterial species, to treat antibiotic-resistant infections..
details.whyItMatters: With antibiotic resistance rising, phage therapy is experiencing a renaissance as a potential solution. It offers the possibility of highly targeted treatments that destroy specific bacteria while leaving beneficial gut flora intact.
takeaways: Bacteriophages infect and kill specific bacterial species with precision
Phages co-evolve with bacteria, potentially countering resistance
Clinical trials are expanding for antibiotic-resistant infections

faq.question: Why was phage therapy abandoned in Western medicine but continued in Eastern Europe?
faq.answer: Western medicine shifted to antibiotics after penicillin's success because antibiotics were easier to manufacture, standardize, and regulate. The Soviet Union and Georgia continued phage research due to limited antibiotic access..

faq.question: What are the main challenges in developing phage therapy for widespread use?
faq.answer: Each phage targets only specific bacterial strains, requiring identification of the infecting strain first. Regulatory frameworks designed for chemical drugs do not easily accommodate evolving biological agents..
